newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts welcome Dresdner funds move.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome Dresdner funds move.

text.p: Analysts on Friday welcomed plans by Germany's Dresdner Bank AG to merge its foreign institutional funds business under one roof as a logical step which should enhance its reputation in fund management.

Dresdner plans to centre its global funds business under U.S. unit RCM Capital Management in a division also including the institutional funds business of London's Kleinwort Benson International Management and the smaller Thornton & Co.
The division will manage assets of more than $50 billion.
"This is a generally positive move. RCM has a very good track record and it makes sense to concentrate control there," said Merck Finck analyst Konrad Becker.

BHF Bank analyst Dieter Hein also said the move was a logical follow-up to Dresdner's acquisition of RCM last year for $300 million, since RCM had the highest level of funds expertise in the Dresdner Bank group.
"Of course this is also part of a trend to centre investment banking outside Germany," he said.
Becker agreed, commenting: "Germany is not where it's at in investment banking. If you want to be a global investment bank, you don't do it from Frankfurt."

However analysts said the move was largely expected and was likley not the main reason for the gains in Dresdner's share price on Friday. The stock was up three percent at 42.85 marks in late bourse trading, while the DAX was up one percent.
A spate of recent "buy" recommendations on Dresdner was largely responsible, analysts said.
Salomon Brothers, London, analyst John Leonard said the Dresdner move was unsurprising, but positive and reminiscent of similar strategies in the past by Swiss Bank Corporation and Barclays Bank.
He also said the move should improve Dresdner's efficiency, especially in terms of co-ordination of marketing activities between RCM and Kleinwort.
Dresdner spokesman Bernd Meyer told Reuters that the merger of the activities should entail some cost savings.
Analysts predicted that RCM would be given a high level of autonomy for Dresdner's global funds business.
BHF Bank analyst Dieter Hein said Dresdner would most likely hold back from imposing direct group control on RCM for fear of alienating key executives and losing valuable clients.
"One of the main advantages in this is RCM's client base. U.S. pension funds in particular are some of the most important clients in fund management," said Merck Finck's Becker.
